text.p: Bear Stearns said it has maintained its attractive rating on Brazilian telecoms operator Telesp following the release of second-quarter earnings.
-- Bear Stearns analysts Rizwan Ali, C.A. Recouso and Daniel Parker said the company reported second-quarter earnings of $4.10 per 1,000 shares compared to $4.00 in the first half of 1996.

-- Revenues increased 23 percent over the same period last year but quarterly operating EBITDA margins contracted to 32 pwercent and 60 percent respectively from 35 percent and 66 percent a year earlier, they said.
-- Wire-line growth in the quarter was ahead of expectations with 89,000 new lines as new higher local call rates gave Telesp incentive to expand its wireline netwwork, they added.
-- Cellular additions fell slightly short of expectations but "we expect more aggressive expansion in the second half of the ywear," the analysts wrote.
-- Tariff rebalancing has made an impact on traffic patterns as local traffic decreased and long-distance traffic rose with lower tariffs, they said.
-- Quarterly results were hurt by Telesp's employee profit-sharing program, which totalled $0.41 per 1,000 shares, they added.

-- Moreover, "Telesp incurred significant non-operating expenses (but) with earnings of $7.89 inthe first half of the year, Telesp is in-line to meet our 1997 earnings estimate of $18.55 for the year.
-- Telepar's preferred closed off 0.57 percent at 349 reais while its common ended up 0.63 percent at 321 reais on the Sao Paulo bourse.
